title: Building Flow: killing a profitable but deceptive subscription while chasing $100M
summary: Episode 2 of Zach's Flow alarm clock build log. He shows launch pain from a subscription upsell, funnel and price A/B tests, and what he learned from advisors. He ends by dropping a profitable subscription model because customers didn't realize they were being subscribed.

principles.text: Don't scale profit built on customers not realizing they're subscribed; protect brand even at a short-term loss.
principles.quote: I don't like that it's deceptive that people are being subscribed without realizing it. So, we're going to the one-time purchase, no subscription model.

principles.text: A bad first-product experience closes the door on future products, so protect the customer experience.
principles.quote: We want to have a bunch of different products for Flow in the future. And if customers have a bad experience with the first one, they're not going to get any in the future.

principles.text: Ship an imperfect v1, then prioritize support and refunds to fix it over time.
principles.quote: they say if you're not embarrassed of what you launch [music] with, you shipped too late.

principles.text: A/B test everything, since tactics that work for others may fail for you.
principles.quote: Some of my websites are doing this and it works really well and even not supplements. So like we had to test it. I don't know why it works for them to be honest.

principles.text: Sending ads to a questionnaire funnel beat sending traffic straight to the product page by about 20%.
principles.quote: going to the funnel was about 20% [music] better with the conversion rate.

principles.text: Build internal metrics early so you aren't flying blind, e.g. activation timing of purchased products.
principles.quote: The bottom line is we're kind of flying an airplane semi-blind right now.
